import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import numpy as np

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Create a comprehensive figure with multiple subplots
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(16, 10))
gs = fig.add_gridspec(3, 3, hspace=0.3, wspace=0.3)

# 1. Price distribution by sensor type
ax1 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, :2])
sensor_order = df.groupby('sensor_type')['price_usd'].median().sort_values(ascending=False).index
sns.boxplot(data=df, x='sensor_type', y='price_usd', order=sensor_order, palette='Set2', ax=ax1)
ax1.set_title('Camera Price Distribution by Sensor Type', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax1.set_xlabel('Sensor Type', fontsize=10)
ax1.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=10)
ax1.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

# 2. 4K video capability over years
ax2 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 2])
video_by_year = df.groupby('model_year')['has_video_4k'].mean() * 100
ax2.plot(video_by_year.index, video_by_year.values, marker='o', linewidth=2, color='#e74c3c')
ax2.fill_between(video_by_year.index, video_by_year.values, alpha=0.3, color='#e74c3c')
ax2.set_title('4K Video Capability Over Time', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax2.set_xlabel('Model Year', fontsize=10)
ax2.set_ylabel('% with 4K Video', fontsize=10)
ax2.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# 3. Price vs Megapixels scatter with sensor type
ax3 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, :2])
sensor_types = df['sensor_type'].unique()
colors = sns.color_palette('husl', len(sensor_types))
for sensor, color in zip(sensor_types, colors):
    mask = df['sensor_type'] == sensor
    ax3.scatter(df[mask]['megapixels'], df[mask]['price_usd'], 
               alpha=0.6, s=50, label=sensor, color=color, edgecolors='black', linewidth=0.5)
ax3.set_title('Price vs Megapixels by Sensor Type', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax3.set_xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=10)
ax3.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=10)
ax3.legend(loc='upper left', fontsize=8, framealpha=0.9)
ax3.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# 4. Top brands by average price
ax4 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 2])
top_brands = df.groupby('brand')['price_usd'].agg(['mean', 'count'])
top_brands = top_brands[top_brands['count'] >= 20].sort_values('mean', ascending=True).tail(8)
ax4.barh(range(len(top_brands)), top_brands['mean'], color='steelblue', edgecolor='black', linewidth=0.5)
ax4.set_yticks(range(len(top_brands)))
ax4.set_yticklabels(top_brands.index, fontsize=9)
ax4.set_title('Top 8 Brands by Avg Price\n(min 20 models)', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax4.set_xlabel('Average Price (USD)', fontsize=10)
ax4.grid(True, alpha=0.3, axis='x')

# 5. Weight vs Price colored by body type
ax5 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, :2])
body_types = df['body_type'].unique()
colors_body = sns.color_palette('Set1', len(body_types))
for body, color in zip(body_types, colors_body):
    mask = df['body_type'] == body
    ax5.scatter(df[mask]['weight_grams'], df[mask]['price_usd'], 
               alpha=0.6, s=50, label=body, color=color, edgecolors='black', linewidth=0.5)
ax5.set_title('Price vs Weight by Body Type', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax5.set_xlabel('Weight (grams)', fontsize=10)
ax5.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=10)
ax5.legend(loc='upper left', fontsize=9, framealpha=0.9)
ax5.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# 6. Max ISO distribution
ax6 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 2])
iso_bins = [0, 6400, 12800, 25600, 51200, df['max_iso'].max()+1]
iso_labels = ['≤6.4K', '6.4-12.8K', '12.8-25.6K', '25.6-51.2K', '>51.2K']
df['iso_category'] = pd.cut(df['max_iso'], bins=iso_bins, labels=iso_labels, include_lowest=True)
iso_counts = df['iso_category'].value_counts().sort_index()
colors_iso = sns.color_palette('YlOrRd', len(iso_counts))
ax6.pie(iso_counts.values, labels=iso_counts.index, autopct='%1.1f%%', 
        colors=colors_iso, startangle=90, textprops={'fontsize': 9})
ax6.set_title('Max ISO Distribution', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')

# Main title
fig.suptitle('Digital Camera Specifications Analysis Dashboard', 
             fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', y=0.995)

# Save figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
